title: The private-name leak scan fails open: a registry that does not load (two roots with one id prefix) gives no private pattern, and file_hits passes every private name
goal: kbcommon's private-name patterns are built, or the leak scan refuses, when the root registry raises RootError, so a clash of id prefixes never lets an internal root's ids, hosts or qualified paths through

run:
import os, sys, tempfile
d = tempfile.mkdtemp(); dirs = []
for name, pre in (("team-x", "TX"), ("team-y", "TY"), ("team-dup", "TX")):
    r = os.path.join(d, name); os.makedirs(r); dirs.append(r)
    open(os.path.join(r, "_root.md"), "w").write(f"---\nroot: {name}\nid_prefix: {pre}\nvisibility: internal\n---\n\n# {name}\n")
os.environ["KB_ROOTS"] = os.pathsep.join(dirs)
sys.path.insert(0, "_tools")
import kbpublic
try:
    h = kbpublic.file_hits("README.md", "see TY-" + "k3f7q2zd and team-y/mdm/x.md", {})
except Exception as e:
    print("refused:", type(e).__name__); sys.exit(0)
print(h); sys.exit(0 if h else 1)
